new_items.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight.
new_items.summary_rss: Elucidating the neural computations underlying natural, complex movement remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Bat flight presents a formidable motor control challenge, requiring hand-like wings whose many degrees of freedom must be precisely coordinated to enable rapid three-dimensional (3D) maneuvers. Here, we performed large-scale wireless recordings from the wing motor cortex of freely flying bats, combined with 3D tracking of wing kinematics. Despite the complexity of flight control, bats repeatedly executed accurate flights through precise adjustments of individual wingbeats. Surprisingly, motor cortical activity was not dominated by the wingbeat cycle. Instead, neurons were sparsely active, exhibiting mixed selectivity for flight kinematics and variable entrainment to the wingbeat phase reaching millisecond-scale precision. This yielded a high-dimensional population code driven by successive wingbeats occupying distinct neural states. These findings reveal a mode of motor cortical population dynamics expressed during natural dexterous movement that is not well captured by prevailing views derived from constrained paradigms.

new_items.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes.
new_items.summary_rss: Structural variants (SVs) are large (>50 base pairs) genomic rearrangements that can significantly influence human phenotypes, yet their contribution to health and disease remains undercharacterized. We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of 1.6 million SVs identified in whole-genome sequencing data from 467,152 UK Biobank participants, across 13,322 binary, 2,018 quantitative, and 2,923 plasma protein traits. Of these, 82.25% of SVs were outside the detectable range of prior copy-number variant studies. Protein quantitative trait loci analysis linked 3,467 SVs to 1,690 proteins, with effects dependent on SV type and location. In SV-PheWAS, we detected 28,184 associations with human health outcomes. Notably, we uncovered rare SVs with strong phenotypic effects. Furthermore, we show that at known genome-wide association study loci, 32.21% of associated SVs overlapped functional genomic regions. This study underscores the underestimated role of SVs in human genetics and their potential to advance understanding of human biology and drug discovery.

new_items.title: A pseudoenzyme sensor of trehalose-6-phosphate directly represses the metabolic integrator SnRK1 in plants.
new_items.summary_rss: Trehalose-6-phosphate (T6P) is a central metabolic signal linking sugar availability to plant growth, carbon utilization, and productivity, yet its sensing and signaling mechanisms remain elusive. Using chemical biology and functional approaches, we identify the noncatalytic pseudoenzyme Class-II T6P synthase (TPS-II) as a T6P sensor in Arabidopsis. In the apo state, TPS-II dimerizes to form an autoinhibitory inter-subunit interaction. T6P binding to the N-terminal TPS-like domain triggers a conformational change that releases the C-terminal domain, enabling interaction with the central metabolic integrator SNF1-related protein kinase 1 (SnRK1) to repress its kinase activity. Loss of TPS-II genes activates catabolic and stress-responsive programs while suppressing anabolic gene expression, consistent with constitutive SnRK1 activity. Conservation of this T6P-TPS-II-SnRK1 signaling axis throughout the plant kingdom highlights its fundamental role in coupling carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis. These findings resolve a long-standing question in sugar signaling and provide a framework for improving crop carbon-use efficiency.

new_items.title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia.
new_items.summary_rss: The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is a major target for pain treatment, but its effectiveness is limited by dangerous side effects. However, the systemic administration of opioids makes it difficult both to decipher their underlying mechanisms of action and to limit drug action to specific receptor subpopulations to isolate therapeutic effects from adverse effects. Here, we develop a reversibly photoswitchable morphinan agonist termed "azo-morphine-3" (AM-3) that interconverts from low to high efficacy in response to light to enable optical control of MOR signaling. Structural analysis of the low ("trans") and high ("cis") efficacy states of AM-3 bound to the MOR reveals distinct binding modes, with each state driving unique ligand, receptor, and G protein dynamics. In mice, AM-3 drives reversible and repeatable optical control of antinociception across pain models with a reduced side effect profile owing to its limited brain accumulation and its ability to be locally activated.

new_items.title: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation.
new_items.summary_rss: Self-organization generates cellular patterns that guide morphogenesis, but how it regulates collective cell fate remains underexplored. We show that cellular self-organization constrains the propagation of ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of oxidative cell death that can otherwise spread as unbounded trigger waves. The spatial patterning of cell density and alignment encodes transcriptional programs, priming cells toward ferroptosis-sensitive or -resistant fates. Low-density, misaligned regions with elevated YAP/TEAD1 activity are sensitive, whereas high-density, aligned regions with increased NRF2 expression form propagation-resistant boundaries. Cell elongation establishes a polarized distribution of oxidizable lipids, creating peroxidation hotspots at the cell poles that promote propagation along cell alignment. In silico and pharmacological perturbations reveal that pattern-dependent susceptibility and polarized lipid organization act together to constrain isotropic waves into spatially confined, anisotropic propagation. These findings identify self-organization as a systems-level mechanism governing collective homeostasis, providing a paradigm to explore how tissue-scale organization regulates cell death in development and disease.

new_items.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing.
new_items.summary_rss: Coleoid cephalopods exhibit the highest levels of adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADAR)-mediated RNA editing of any known taxon, yet the functional consequences of most recoding events remain unclear. Here, we integrated proteomics with biochemical and cellular assays to characterize recoding across the Doryteuthis pealeii proteome. This confirmed the translation of 7,997 recoded sites at the protein level and revealed how recoding reshapes the proteome by altering protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modifications, and enzymatic activity. We find that recoding also creates or ablates post-translational modification sites, with direct effects on protein function and protein-protein interactions. Recoding the E3 ligase MARCHF5 drives widespread changes in substrate ubiquitylation and perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis, illustrating how RNA editing can influence organelle function. Together, these data give a proteome-scale view of how extensive RNA recoding diversifies protein function in coleoid cephalopods and offer a framework for understanding how RNA-level plasticity shapes protein function and cellular physiology.

new_items.title: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy.
new_items.summary_rss: Distal enhancers activate genes over vast genomic distances, but how this communication occurs and what signals are transmitted are poorly understood. Using real-time single-gene nanoscopy and targeted perturbations, we define physical parameters and mechanisms of enhancer-promoter communication. We find that productive interactions are dynamic, occur at a proximity of ≲100 nm, and are coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Enhancers and promoters find one another not only through passive diffusion; we often directly observe them being actively brought together by cohesin-mediated loop extrusion, which is a key determinant of transcriptional burst frequency. We also discover that specific general transcription factors (GTFs) of RNA polymerase II machinery are key to initiating transcriptional bursts, and enhancer-promoter interactions activate bursting by embedding the promoter within GTF clusters that form at the enhancers. Our results resolve the molecular and biochemical signals involved in long-range gene activation and elucidate the biophysical mechanisms for their transmission from the enhancer to the promoter.

new_items.title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression.
new_items.summary_rss: Ferroptosis is implicated as a vulnerability in multiple cancers, yet approaches for effectively inducing ferroptosis in vivo are limited. Bypassing conventional strategies targeting the antiferroptotic glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) proteins, we designed metabolic initiators of lipid peroxidation (MILPOs) and developed the compounds WMK-1/2, which contain tetraoxane radical-generating and mitochondria-targeting groups, as de novo ferroptosis inducers. WMK-1 localizes primarily to mitochondria, induces local lipid peroxidation, and impairs oxidative phosphorylation. WMK-1 induces a "mito-ferroptosis" sub-pathway that skips GPX4 inhibition as a prerequisite, can be rescued by lipophilic radical-trapping antioxidants, yet is minimally sensitive to acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) perturbation and long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation, and evades retinol-mediated protection. Instead, WMK-1-induced cell death requires labile Fe 2+ and can be selectively suppressed by ɑ-lipoic acid, an endogenous, mitochondria-resident antioxidant. WMK-1/2 are bioavailable and exhibit significant efficacy in tumor suppression by eliciting ferroptosis in multiple cancer models and augmenting the antitumor effects of immune-checkpoint blockers. Our work provides a protein-targeting-independent metabolic ferroptosis induction strategy for potential cancer therapy.

new_items.title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise.
new_items.summary_rss: Exercise reduces all-cause mortality, yet its molecular effects across organs, sexes, and circadian phases remain incompletely understood. We subjected mice to 8 weeks of voluntary wheel running and collected 22 tissues and plasma during active and inactive phases for bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, and single-nucleus RNA and methylation sequencing. Exercise induced canonical fiber-type switching and widespread, tissue-specific remodeling, with the largest transcriptomic changes in skeletal muscle. Except for the hypothalamus, kidney, and lung, most tissues changed more during the active phase. Females showed broader transcriptional responses, with distinct downregulation. Pairing single-nucleus methylomes with transcriptomes resolved the cell types driving exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling-changes undetectable by bulk studies. These included coordinated gene-body demethylation and transcription that tracked with fiber-type switching in specific myonuclei. Cell-type-resolved methylation, including partially methylated domains characterized in muscle, revealed a strong, sex-biased epigenetic response to training. Machine learning identified conserved exercise signatures across mammalian species.

new_items.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system.
new_items.summary_rss: Tetanus neurotoxin (TeNT) invades the central nervous system (CNS) via retrograde transport through motoneurons. Whether a host factor is needed to mediate TeNT trafficking has remained unknown. Here, using pull-down and mass spectrometry analysis, and by developing a luciferase-based in vivo transport assay, we identify receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase sigma (PTPRS; PTPσ) as the retrograde transport receptor for TeNT. Global or motoneuron-specific PTPRS knockout (KO) abolishes TeNT entry into the CNS in mouse models. PTPRS-TeNT interactions occur in endosomes, prevent toxin translocation, and direct TeNT trafficking in neurons. Structural studies establish that the TeNT light chain and belt region bind to the immunoglobulin domain of PTPRS. Disrupting TeNT-PTPRS interactions blocks TeNT trafficking into the spinal cord; consistently, a PTPRS-binding-deficient TeNT mutant induces botulism-like flaccid paralysis. Thus, PTPRS is the host factor mediating TeNT trafficking into the CNS, revealing a targetable pathway for post-entry intervention and drug delivery into the CNS.

new_items.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations.
new_items.summary_rss: Human centromeres are highly variable but remain among the least characterized regions of the genome because their repetitive structure has hindered conventional analysis of population diversity and disease relevance. Here, we show that rare k-mers in centromeric regions capture lineage-specific variation, defining discrete haplogroups with distinct structural features. We developed ascairn to infer these haplogroups from short-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. Applying this framework to >3,300 genomes reveals extensive global diversity in centromere haplogroups and signatures of population history. Analyzing short-read WGS data from 142 oligodendroglioma cases with 1p/19q co-deletion, we mapped breakpoints to the centromere regions of chromosomes 1 and 19, revealing a clear positional relationship to kinetochore attachment sites and a link between centromere haplotype structure and rearrangement susceptibility. Rare k-mers thus open centromeres to population-scale analysis, linking centromere structural diversity to human evolutionary history and disease-associated genomic instability.

Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3.
new_items.summary_rss: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

new_items.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor.
new_items.summary_rss: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal's assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing's most important challenges.
